questions.stem: The SPA switches from sending the ID token to the access token. The tenant_id claim, added by a pre token generation trigger, disappears. Most likely cause?
options: The JWT authorizer strips custom claims
The trigger uses event version V1_0, which customizes only the ID token; access token customization needs V2_0 (or later)
Access tokens never carry custom claims
The app client lacks the openid scope
questions.explanation: Version 1 events can only change ID token claims. Version 2 adds claimsAndScopeOverrideDetails with accessTokenGeneration. The docs tie access token customization to the Essentials or Plus feature plan.

questions.stem: Where does a V2_0 pre token generation trigger put a claim for both tokens?
options: event.response.claimsOverrideDetails.claimsToAddOrOverride
event.response.claimsAndScopeOverrideDetails.idTokenGeneration and .accessTokenGeneration, each with claimsToAddOrOverride
event.request.userAttributes
A return value of {"claims": {...}}
questions.explanation: V2 responses use claimsAndScopeOverrideDetails with separate idTokenGeneration and accessTokenGeneration sections (the access token section can also add or suppress scopes). claimsOverrideDetails is the V1 shape.

questions.stem: Your Lambda behind an HTTP API JWT authorizer must decide the tenant. Which are correct? Choose two.
options: Read it from requestContext.authorizer.jwt.claims, which API Gateway populated after validating the token
Prefer a tenant_id query parameter when present because it is more specific
If the claim is missing, return 403 instead of falling back to a default tenant
Decode the token again and trust the payload without validation
Use the user's email domain as the tenant
questions.explanation: The authorizer validated issuer, audience and signature, so its claims are the trusted source. Defaults and request parameters turn a missing claim into cross-tenant access (w4-t1).

questions.stem: An identity policy uses ForAllValues:StringLike on dynamodb:LeadingKeys with TENANT#${aws:PrincipalTag/tenant_id} and allows GetItem, Query and Scan. What is wrong?
options: Nothing
Scan has no leading keys; ForAllValues over an empty set evaluates to true, so Scan reads every tenant's items
StringLike cannot use policy variables
LeadingKeys only works with ForAnyValue
questions.explanation: ForAllValues is true when the request carries no values for the key. Scan provides no leading keys, so the condition passes. Drop Scan from tenant roles; ForAnyValue would be wrong for BatchGetItem with mixed keys.

questions.stem: How does a tool Lambda get a session whose ABAC policy keys on aws:PrincipalTag/tenant_id?
options: Set an environment variable TENANT_ID
Call sts:AssumeRole with Tags=[{Key: tenant_id, Value: <verified tenant>}] (the role trust policy must allow sts:TagSession)
Add the tag to the Lambda function
Put the tenant in the RoleSessionName
questions.explanation: Session tags passed on AssumeRole become principal tags for that session. The trust policy must allow sts:TagSession. Function tags are resource tags, not principal tags of the execution role session.

questions.stem: Which multi-tenant Cognito models are described as options, with trade-offs? Choose two.
options: One user pool with a tenant attribute or group per tenant
A separate user pool per tenant for stronger isolation and per-tenant settings
One IAM user per end user
Sharing a single Cognito user across tenants
Storing passwords in DynamoDB per tenant
questions.explanation: The Cognito multi-tenant guidance covers attribute- or group-based models in one pool, app client per tenant, and pool per tenant, trading isolation and per-tenant configuration against operational overhead.

questions.stem: Brightline wants its employees to sign in with their corporate IdP. Which Cognito feature fits a B2B tenant?
options: An identity pool unauthenticated role
A SAML or OIDC identity provider federated into the user pool, mapped to that tenant
A user pool group named after the IdP
Custom authentication challenge triggers
questions.explanation: User pools federate SAML and OIDC IdPs; a per-tenant IdP plus a mapping to the tenant (attribute or lookup in the trigger) is the usual B2B pattern.

questions.stem: Access patterns: get ticket by id, list a tenant's open tickets newest first, list a tenant's tickets for a shipment. Which design fits single-table modeling best?
options: pk = ticket id; scan with a filter on tenant
pk = TENANT#t, sk = TICKET#id; GSI1 pk = TENANT#t#STATUS#s, sk = created_at; GSI2 pk = TENANT#t#SHIPMENT#id
One table per tenant with a scan per query
pk = status, sk = tenant
questions.explanation: Design from access patterns: every pattern becomes a GetItem or Query, every partition key is tenant-prefixed (which also enables LeadingKeys), and no pattern needs Scan.

questions.stem: Why is a tenant id as the leading part of every partition key useful? Choose two.
options: IAM dynamodb:LeadingKeys can restrict a session to its tenant's items
Queries for one tenant never touch another tenant's partition
It guarantees even partition load for very large tenants
It removes the need for application tests
It makes Scan cheaper
questions.explanation: Tenant-prefixed keys make isolation enforceable below the application and keep queries scoped. A very large tenant can still create a hot partition, so high-volume items may need write sharding.

questions.stem: Another tenant's ticket id is requested with a valid token. Why return 404 rather than 403?
options: 404 is cheaper
The key is built from the caller's tenant, so for them the item does not exist; 403 would confirm that the id exists for someone else
403 cannot be returned by an HTTP API
Clients retry 403 automatically
questions.explanation: Returning 403 leaks existence (an enumeration oracle). Building the key from the verified tenant makes 404 the natural, honest answer.

questions.stem: Per-user rules such as 'a clinic manager may approve refunds under 500 only for their own clinics' are growing in the tool Lambdas. Which AWS service is designed for this?
options: IAM permission boundaries
Amazon Verified Permissions with Cedar policies
Cognito groups only
AWS WAF
questions.explanation: Verified Permissions evaluates Cedar policies for fine-grained application authorization, keeping rules out of tool code. IAM still guards AWS resources underneath.

questions.stem: Which statements about Cognito identity pools in this architecture are correct? Choose two.
options: They exchange a user pool token for temporary AWS credentials
Role-based access control can map token claims or groups to IAM roles
They replace the need for a user pool for sign-in
They issue the JWT that API Gateway validates
They store tenant data
questions.explanation: Identity pools give temporary AWS credentials and can choose roles from token claims; sign-in and JWTs come from the user pool.
